ops.title: Fresh Sprite startup: pinned SquashFS tool payload design (fresh-startup-92s)
ops.body:
Decision (2026-10-02, lane fresh-startup-92s, root-directed): fresh Sprites get prepared tools from a credential-free, pinned SquashFS payload that is mounted read-only through the kernel loop driver. No FUSE.

- Build: render the inventory with private marketplaces removed (`Inventory.Public()`). Run the unchanged installer on a fresh build Sprite, then `provision.sh pack` creates the zstd squashfs from an allowlist of trees.
- Consume: `provision.sh payload URL SHA256` downloads and verifies the image into `/var/lib/cc-remote/payload/<sha>.sqfs` and mounts it at `/opt/cc-remote/payload/<sha>`. A root sprite-env service, `cc-remote-payload`, checks the sha256 before each boot-time mount. `expose` links or copies trees so the existing digest/ref/version/registry fast paths hit. Absent or stale entries install live through the same code.
- Exposure rules come from source audits:
  - Claude plugin cache uses **leaf** version links.
  - Captain Hook's `<Build>` dir stays real, with its children linked.
  - `/opt/uv/python` is linked as a whole root; each `/opt/uv/tools/<name>` is linked separately.
  - Codex plugin store and `config.toml` are copied.
  - Registries and `settings.json` are copied as private files.
- Schedule: live APT runs as its own lane, overlapped with checkout and with the tools → configure → enroll lane. The readiness stamp is published only after every lane succeeds.

Probe evidence: `setup-20261001/fresh-startup-92s-mount-probe-cc-remote-mount-probe-eedd5c92`. Full contract: `setup-20261001/fresh-startup-92s-result.json` `implementationContract`. Tree audit: `setup-20261001/fresh-startup-92s-tree-audit.txt`.
